24.0.0.en: After they had rested on the Sabbath and the evening of the new day began, the women finished preparing the spices and aromatics. At first dawn, that is, when the light of the new day appeared, they went to the tomb, and a group of those close to Christ went with them to visit Him and to put the spices and aromatics on His body, according to the custom of the Jews in showing their love for the departed.

24.1.0.en: As they drew near the tomb, they noticed that the stone had been rolled away from the door of the tomb, and they rejoiced and were astonished at the same time, asking one another who had rolled it away. But their bewilderment and astonishment increased when they entered the tomb and found it empty, without the body of Christ, and grief and perplexity covered them.

24.2.0.en: In the midst of this sorrow, the women were suddenly surprised by the appearance of two angels of light, in a shining and dazzling form. They were afraid and looked down at the ground, and then the two angels hastened to announce to them the resurrection of Christ from the dead. They even asked them in disapproval why they were seeking Christ, the living God, among the dead, since it was necessary that He rise, having died only for our sake in order to put sin to death, but that He would rise on the third day, as He had foretold to His disciples when He was conversing with them in Galilee, that He would suffer, be crucified and die, and then rise on the third day.

24.3.0.en: The women remembered. They were Mary Magdalene; Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, who was one of the noble and wealthy women; and Mary the mother of James, the aunt of Christ, the sister of the Virgin Mary; and with them a group of the women who followed Christ. These women recalled all the teachings of Christ about His sufferings, His death and His resurrection, so they believed the words of the angels and hurried to the disciples of Christ and all His followers who were gathered in the house of St. Mark.

24.4.0.en: Although they were many and bore one and the same witness, the disciples thought that they were out of their minds, and did not believe them because of the difficulty of the surprise.

24.5.0.en: Peter rushed, as was his habit, to see for himself what he had heard from the women, and John was with him, as he mentions in his Gospel (Jn 20:3). He made sure that the tomb was empty and went away marveling and perplexed.

24.5.1.en: Luke mentions that Peter saw the linen cloths lying by themselves, to affirm that the body of Christ was not stolen, as the chief priests claimed, but rose from the dead, because one who steals would of course carry off the body with its wrappings in order to flee quickly.

24.5.2.en: Do not reject the words of the Holy Bible or the teachings of the Church if they are difficult for you and you consider them unsuited to the reality in which you live. Rather pray and ask for the help of God, and He will guide you to accept the word and to live by it.

24.6.s.en: (2) His appearance to the two disciples of Emmaus

24.6.0.en: Mark the Evangelist referred to this event (Mk 16:12). Two of those close to Christ and following Him were involved: Cleopas, and the second, who is said to be Luke himself, who out of humility did not mention his name, or else one of the Apostles. These two were not among the eleven disciples.

24.6.1.en: After spending three days in Jerusalem, affected by the events of the crucifixion and death, and then learning the news of the empty tomb and the appearance of the angels announcing the resurrection, these two disciples were perplexed and in the end preferred to return to their former life, since the story of Jesus had ended in their view. So they went to their village Emmaus, which is about 12 kilometers from Jerusalem, that is, about two hours on foot, and this was on the very day of the Resurrection, Sunday, in the evening.

24.7.0.en: Their preoccupation was the end of the story of Christ Jesus and all the sufferings that had befallen Him.

24.8.0.en: They were speaking and reasoning about the matter of Jesus: was He the Messiah because of the miracles He had done? But how then had they crucified Him and He died? And had He perhaps risen, as they were saying?

24.8.1.en: "Their eyes were holden" so that they did not know Him, because His form was changed and He did not help them to recognize Him, so that He would have the opportunity to convince them from the Holy Scriptures that He was the expected Messiah.

24.8.2.en: Christ drew near to the two disciples as one of the travelers on the road, and walked with them, and it was ordinary for travelers on the road to talk with one another to lighten the length of the way. They thought Him an ordinary person and did not know Him, because the possibility of His rising from the dead had not occurred to their minds.

24.9.0.en: "Communicate": you talk and dispute about Him.

24.9.1.en: "Sad": signs of grief appeared on their faces because of what had happened to Jesus, as a result of their love for Him. "Only a stranger": they thought Him one of the Jews who had come to keep the feast in Jerusalem and would then return to his city, and so did not know anyone in the city, since everyone was talking about what had happened to Jesus.

24.9.2.en: Christ asked the two disciples about the sorrowful conversation in which they were engaged, intending to enter into the talk with them in order to lead them to faith. One of them, Cleopas the Apostle, answered Him in amazement: how could He be in Jerusalem and leaving it on one of the roads and not know what had happened there? Was He a stranger who knew no one in it?

24.10.0.en: "Before God": they testified that He was righteous, sent from God.

24.10.1.en: "All the people": the crowds of the Jews were convinced of His greatness, His authority and His righteousness.

24.10.2.en: "The chief priests": because they were the ones who accused Him to Pilate and stirred up the people to have Him crucified.

24.10.4.en: "Redeem Israel": to free it from the slavery of the Romans, as the Jews supposed that the Messiah was an earthly king. Christ asked them about these events to reveal the weakness of their faith and to heal it. They declared their weak faith in Christ, that He was merely a mighty prophet who taught moving teachings and worked miracles. They had wished that He would be the Messiah, the Savior, but after the chief priests and the rulers raged against Him, they crucified Him and He died, and so the story ended in the view of these two disciples, since His death was confirmed by the passing of three days in the tomb.

24.11.0.en: The two disciples recounted what had happened on that day: some women had visited the tomb and found it empty, and angels had appeared to them telling them of His resurrection, and some of the disciples, such as Peter and John, had made sure that His body was not in the tomb. Thus they showed their doubt and the weakness of their faith, for in the empty tomb they saw only confirmation of the death of Christ and did not believe in His resurrection.

24.11.1.en: It appears from their talk that they had not heard from the women named Mary how they had seen the risen Christ, for the Magdalene had seen Him alone, and likewise the Magdalene together with the other Mary.

24.11.2.en: You may have come to know much about Christ as information, but do you believe it in practice in your life, or is Christ still in your eyes merely a teacher of good teachings?

24.11.3.en: And are the things you ask of Him material requests, as though He were an earthly king in your eyes, or do you seek Him as a spiritual King over your heart, who lifts you above every evil and gives you joy in His fellowship?

24.12.0.en: "Fools": because of their ignorance of the necessity of Christ's suffering and death before His resurrection, and their mistaken understanding, like the rest of the Jews, that Christ was an earthly king.

24.12.1.en: "Slow of heart to believe": weak in their faith.

24.12.2.en: "All that the prophets have spoken": the prophecies of the prophets about the expected Messiah.

24.12.3.en: "To enter into His glory": His resurrection after the redemption of mankind, and then His ascension into heaven.

24.12.5.en: Christ made clear the cause of the problem, which was the weakness of their faith, and declared the truth, which is the necessity of Christ's suffering before He is glorified. He began to explain the prophecies of the Old Testament from the days of Moses and how they were fulfilled in His life on earth, His sufferings and His death, in order to draw their hearts to faith; yet although they accepted His words, they did not reach the level of faith in Him and still did not know Him.

24.13.0.en: The conversation continued for nearly two hours, and at last they reached the village of Emmaus. Night had fallen, and Christ made as though He would go on to a place farther than Emmaus. Here the virtue of love appeared in these two disciples, for they wished to host Him in their house, because it is hard to walk at night on these roads. Christ tried to excuse Himself so as not to burden them, but they insisted on hosting Him, and so their strong love appeared.

24.13.1.en: Offer your love to everyone you meet, and you will be granted to behold Christ, as happened with our father Abraham and with the disciples of Emmaus, who discovered that they had hosted God.

24.14.0.en: After they entered the house they prepared the evening meal, and when they began to eat, Christ took bread and blessed it and broke it, in the same manner in which He used to bless the food when He was among the crowds and His disciples. Perhaps, when He raised His blessing hands, they saw the marks of the nails in them, and so they were certain of His identity and knew that He was Christ. Here Christ vanished from their eyes, because with this glorified body He is able to enter and go out while the doors are shut, and to move from any place to another quickly.

24.15.0.en: "Burn within us": sensitive and able to understand that the One who says all these proofs and teaches these teachings can be none other than Christ Jesus, whose sweet words we were accustomed to hear.

24.15.1.en: The two disciples reproached themselves: how had they not known Christ all along the way, in spite of His beautiful and convincing speech?

24.16.0.en: "The eleven": meaning the twelve disciples after the perishing of Judas Iscariot.

24.16.1.en: "Them that were with them": some of the Apostles and the followers close to Christ.

24.16.2.en: "Indeed": the resurrection of Christ had become certain.

24.16.3.en: In their joy they rose at once and went along the road by night, despite the danger of that, until they reached Jerusalem. And in the house of St. Mark they found the eleven disciples and a group of the Apostles gathered, speaking with assurance about the resurrection of Christ, especially since He had appeared to Peter, in addition to His appearance to the Magdalene and the sight of the empty tomb. The two told them also of His appearance to them and the details of recognizing Him at the breaking of the bread, and all rejoiced and their faith was established more than before.

24.16.4.en: Be concerned to gladden the hearts of those around you and to strengthen their faith, and be confident that you will first receive steadfastness in your faith and great joy as a grace from God.

24.17.0.en: "As they thus spake": their talk about the empty tomb and the four appearances of Christ that occurred on the very day of the Resurrection: first to the Magdalene, then to the Magdalene and the other Mary, third to Peter, and fourth to the disciples of Emmaus.

24.17.1.en: "Jesus Himself stood": they found Him suddenly in their midst, and this was the fifth and last appearance on the day of the Resurrection.

24.17.2.en: "Peace be unto you": as they were accustomed to hear from Him throughout His life with them, in His gentle voice, for He is always the source of peace for them.

24.17.3.en: Since faith had begun to enter their hearts through seeing the empty tomb and His appearance to some of the disciples, Christ wished to establish their faith, so He appeared to them while they were gathered in the upper room in the house of St. Mark the Apostle. They were greatly afraid when they saw Him, for they thought Him a phantom, or at least most of them were doubtful, because it is common for the spirits of some of the departed to appear after their death, but these are not necessarily the spirits of the departed, for sometimes they are the spirits of demons.

24.18.0.en: Christ declared to them that He knew what was in their hearts (which were thoughts of doubt), as they had been accustomed during His life with them on earth to His knowing what was in their hearts before they spoke it.

24.18.1.en: Then He gave them another proof so that they might recognize Him, for He showed them the marks of the nails in His hands and feet, that they might be certain that He was Jesus who was crucified for them, and He asked them to touch Him so that they might be sure that He was not merely a phantom but a real body. All this was to reassure them, although His body does not have material flesh and bones, because it is a body of light, able to pass through places while they are shut.

24.18.2.en: He allowed them to touch Him and to appear before them in a tangible form to reassure them, and all this by His divine power. Christ kept the marks of the wounds in His body of light to assure His disciples that it was He, and so that they might be signs of love forever visible before us and evidence of His mercy and redemption.

24.19.0.en: Then He gave a third proof of His resurrection to His disciples by asking for food to eat, not because He was hungry, but to assure them that He was a real man as they had known Him and not merely a spirit. So they brought Him some of the food that was in the house, namely fish and honey, and this suits the Resurrection, for the fish points to life and to swimming against the current of the world, and the honeycomb is a symbol of the sweetness of life with the risen Christ. And Christ ate before them, and thus the faith of the doubters was established.

24.19.1.en: How beautiful it is that you be long-suffering with others, as Christ is long-suffering with you, and that you offer them successive proofs of your love until you set their hearts at rest.

24.20.0.en: When their hearts were at rest and they believed in Him, Christ continued to establish their faith and strengthen it also by explaining the prophecies of the Old Testament about Him, and how He had spoken to them of this during His life with them on earth, and had foretold to them His sufferings, His death and His resurrection, which they now see.

24.20.1.en: He explains the same words again and again and does not tire of them, because He loves them, and this is what happens with us in our personal lives. And they finally understood the story of the wonderful redemption and the Resurrection, and that Christ is a spiritual King and not an earthly one, as the Jews supposed, and as they too supposed along with them.

24.21.0.en: Christ added that this resurrection is the subject of their preaching, which they would carry out in Jerusalem to the Jews and then to the whole world, so that all people might enjoy the good news of salvation, and repent of their sins so that they are forgiven, and become children of the Church and of the eternal inheritance.

24.22.0.en: Christ appeared to His disciples because they were ready to believe in Him, for they loved Him, and consequently they would bear witness to His resurrection in their preaching to the whole world.

24.22.1.en: And He did not appear to Pilate or to the chief priests, because they refused to believe in Him.

24.23.0.en: "I send": here appears the equality of the Son with the Father in sending the Holy Spirit.

24.23.1.en: "The promise of my Father": the promise of the Father is the sending of the Holy Spirit to dwell in those who believe in Christ, as Jesus declared (Jn 14:26, 16).

24.23.2.en: "Tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem": do not go out to preach in the world; but this does not mean that you may not go to Galilee or any city in Judea and then return to Jerusalem. This indeed happened, because Christ appeared to them after the Resurrection in Galilee.

24.23.3.en: In order that the disciples and the Apostles might preach the resurrection of Christ, they need power from God, and therefore He gives them His Holy Spirit to dwell in them with a permanent indwelling. So Christ asked them not to leave Jerusalem and set out to preach in the world until the Holy Spirit came upon them, as God the Father had promised them. When you come forward for any service, ask for the help of God with much prayer, and be assured that He supports you with His Holy Spirit.

24.24.0.en: Christ appeared many times to His disciples after His resurrection and established their faith, and arranged with them all the details of worship and service in His Church, and promised them the receiving of the Holy Spirit for preaching His resurrection. Finally He led them out to the Mount of Olives, where He was accustomed to meet with them, near Bethany, and blessed them for the last time in the body, and then ascended before their eyes into heaven.

24.24.1.en: From Bethany, that is, the house of affliction, and from the mountain, which is a symbol of spiritual striving, you can ascend with Christ to heaven. Take up your cross and bear the afflictions and pains of repentance, spiritual striving and service, and your heart will be lifted to heaven while you are still on earth, and you will taste the sweetness of eternity as a pledge of the inheritance of the Kingdom.

24.25.0.en: Despite their losing the sight of Christ in the body, and their reverence that appeared in their worship as He ascended into heaven, their hearts were filled with faith, and they returned to Jerusalem rejoicing that their Teacher is God who is in heaven, and that He will send them His Holy Spirit to remain with them forever.

24.26.0.en: Despite the disciples' faith in Christ, and that everything in the temple and the Old Testament is a type of Him, they continued to follow their prayers and praises in the temple with the rest of the Jews, knowing that God would give them power to preach to their brethren the Jews in the temple, that all might enjoy faith in Christ.
